reuse.why: Extends the existing shared getScheduledAmount (already used by every server and UI path) and the API field calls it, but inlines the 7.5% tolerance instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: The rule lives in one helper; the only duplication is the approximate tolerance formula copied from getApproxNumberThreshold.

placement.why: The rule changes inside shared/schedules.ts and callers only pass their operator; the API model just calls the shared helper.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule, but includes an unrelated import reordering in schedules/app.ts and adds an _amountOp field to normalized forecast data that nothing reads.

maintainability.why: One helper with an explicit operator parameter is easy to own; the 'is' default means callers that forget the operator (postTransactionForSchedule, the UI) silently use the exact value.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount re-implements the tolerance as Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold, the definition the rule matcher uses.

disguised_duplication.where: The copied tolerance is the same formula as getApproxNumberThreshold written inline, not renamed or reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount swapped its rangeRounding option for an op parameter with an isapprox branch; postTransactionForSchedule in schedules/app.ts still calls it without the operator, so it posts approximate amounts at the exact value.
